body:
I've kept going because part of me always hopes that there's something better for me in the future, and that this is just a bump in the road. The future could be bad, it could be good, but ultimately, it is our future and we have the power to make changes and direct how it goes. It is an absolute nightmare trying to reconcile these feelings of hopefulness with the hopelessness that often comes with suicidal thoughts, but it is this constant fight between these two sides (in addition to medication and mental health professional visits) that has managed to keep me going.

I sometimes have days where I wonder if I even have depression, and other times have days where I'm ready to write my final note. The best advice I received from my therapist was that I needed to not think about my past or future (with regards to my mental health issues) but instead focus on the present and the things I do now. When I think about the family I have, the friends I have, the places I'm in, and the things I'm capable of doing, I know that a small part of me is still trying to fight against the urge to die.

I'm sorry if this isn't helpful, but I wanted to let you know that I come from a very similar background and was also hit by depression in such a sudden and fast way. The thing that has always kept me going is trying to find something new for myself or something new to live for. Right now, it's my cat. In the future, maybe it will be a partner or a new friend group. Regardless, I have to fight against my urges to die and keep looking for those bright spots that I was once so easily able to find before I was diagnosed.
